label: conj:symmetric-crystal-pair-production
title: Type-B folding forces matter/antimatter to be created in conjugate-operator pairs
html:
Conjecture (symmetric-crystal pair production). Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of type A_{n-1} with Hecke normal forms \{T_w\}. Let \mathrm{Cryst}(\mathfrak{sl}_n) be its associated Kashiwara crystal. Fold the \mathfrak{sl}_n Cartan datum into a Type B Cartan datum along the Dynkin involution i \mapsto \bar i = n - i. Equivalently, apply the \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} bar-involution T_w \mapsto \overline{T_w} that sends q \mapsto q^{-1} and reverses crossings. The resulting symmetric crystal \mathrm{Cryst}^{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}) admits no Kashiwara lowering operator \tilde f_i as a unimodal step from a bar-invariant source. Every step is a paired operator (\tilde f_i, \tilde f_{\bar i}). Consequently, a transition

  v_0 \;\xrightarrow{\;(\tilde f_i, \tilde f_{\bar i})\;}\; v_-\,\sqcup\,v_+,

from a bar-invariant highest-weight vector v_0 produces two descendants v_-, v_+ whose Hecke normal forms are bar-conjugates (\overline{T_{v_-}} = T_{v_+}). We identify v_- with a chiral particle and v_+ with its CPT antiparticle. The symmetric crystal forbids the production of a single chiral excitation from a non-chiral source. Any descendant set is a disjoint union of bar-conjugate pairs.

Algorithmic role (charge-conservation kill switch). The Gröbner–Shirshov reduction engine enforces matter–antimatter pairing structurally. At each crystal step, it applies the folded operator pair atomically. An internally generated intermediate carrying a single net chirality is unreachable. The Hecke normal forms produced by the engine are bar-invariant by construction. The engine rejects any candidate normal form failing this test before further expansion. This converts CPT and charge conservation from combinatorial post-conditions into intrinsic invariants of the crystal traversal. No custom \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} rules are required.

Conjectural status. The Type B folding of \mathfrak{sl}_n Kashiwara crystals into \mathfrak{so}_{2n+1} symmetric crystals is established at the level of generic quantum-group representations. The bar-involution is intrinsic to the KLR canonical basis. We conjecture that the folded operators on the cyclotomic quotient realising H_n(R, q) realise exactly the matter/antimatter pairing of the topological ansatz. The bar-conjugate pair on a single Type B crystal node corresponds to a CPT pair of QOU particles. The empirical evidence is the \det \rho_\lambda(w) \cdot \det \rho_{\lambda'}(w) = \pm 1 identity for every conjugate-partition pair (\lambda, \lambda'). This identity is the bar-involution acting on Wedderburn blocks.
